test: live backend-to-PostgreSQL network partition with owner process kept alive
environment: isolated local Docker Compose project; PostgreSQL 16; two backend processes; per-node TCP DB proxies; TLS Nginx; loopback ports; temporary synthetic users and lesson
scope_and_limits: Repeated after the durable event-ack staging change. All existing role channels received the fencing event and closed; the old backend process remained running and healthy while it had no PostgreSQL route. The other node claimed the expired lease and restored the checkpoint in 10.68 seconds. After the DB route was restored, the old node rejected a direct control handshake with HTTP 403. Through TLS Nginx the REST and four WS channels reached the recovered session on their first retry. Test users/session/audit rows and the isolated Compose volumes were removed. This did not drive business commands during the partition or prove zero loss/duplication for commands racing checkpoint commit; no target-hardware or failure-overlap load was run. Reproduce with scripts/test_cluster_failover.py --failure-mode partition and docker-compose.partition-test.yml.
